title: One-step CNF replaceability for a layer of DNF gates
statement:
Fix layer-2 data over $n \ge 1$ variables: a family of $m$ DNF gates $G_1, \dots, G_m$ together with a common width bound $w > 0$ satisfying $\mathrm{width}(G_i) \le w$ for every $i$. Let $l \in \bbn$ and let $p \in \bbr$ satisfy $0 < p \le \tfrac{1}{40\,w}$ and $p \le 1$. Then, under a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction $\rho$ on the $n$ variables, the probability that some gate fails the property — that is, the probability that it is *not* the case that for every $i$ the restricted function $x \mapsto G_i(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ agrees, on all inputs, with some CNF formula of width at most $l$ — is at most
\[
  m\left(\left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{l} + \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{n p}{3}\right)\right).
\]
hypotheses_covered: common width bound width > 0 with each gate's width ≤ width (from the layer-2 data)
replaced:
For layer-2 data and a Bernoulli parameter $p$ with $0<p\le 1/(40\cdot\mathrm{width})$ and
$p\le 1$, the probability that it fails that every gate's restricted function is computed by
some width-$l$ CNF is at most
\[
  \mathrm{numGates}\cdot\left((1/2)^{l} + \exp(-np/3)\right).
\]
